title: Elodie and the Signal
premise: Ansel Montrose, the last human technician aboard the automated relay station Vesper Gate, maintains a network of worlds that fell silent decades ago. When a deep-space survey ship returns with its crew aged backward into children who remember their own futures, Ansel discovers the anomaly is a signal — a message folded through time by the relay at the edge of dead space, where something has been listening. Racing a closing jump window, Ansel and Elodie, the ship's de-aged captain who remembers loving him in a future that no longer exists, must decide whether to answer the signal or silence it forever, knowing either choice will erase one of their memories of each other.
about_author: Orsen Yarrow is the pen name of a former radio engineer who spent six years maintaining remote communications arrays in the subarctic before turning to fiction. Their work explores loneliness at scale — the quiet heroism of people who keep signals alive for others.

chapters.title: The Long Route
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. A day in the life aboard Vesper Gate: calibrating dead relays, talking to automated voices, logging silence. He reveals his routine is also his prison — he stayed when everyone evacuated. Emotional beat: tender melancholy, a man in love with a job nobody needs done.

chapters.title: Return Vector
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The survey ship Meridian answers no hails but docks on autopilot. Inside: twenty-two crew members aged backward into children, physically eight years old, calm and unnervingly coherent. Emotional beat: dread blooming into wonder as the smallest child calls him by name.

chapters.title: Elodie
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The ship's captain, now a child, explains she remembers a future — including Ansel, including a choice they made together. She doesn't know him yet, but she grieves him like an old friend. Emotional beat: disorienting intimacy; love arriving out of order.

chapters.title: Quarantine of One
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Station protocol demands isolation of the Meridian crew; Ansel instead feeds them, breaks his own rules, and listens. The children describe dying in deep space and waking younger. Emotional beat: guilt and warmth colliding as duty frays against compassion.

chapters.title: What the Relays Heard
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Reviewing Meridian's flight data, Elodie finds a repeating pattern embedded in relay chatter — a structured signal originating from the edge of dead space, timed to their passage. Emotional beat: cold clarity; the mystery acquires coordinates and teeth.

chapters.title: The Jump Window
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Orbital mechanics give them one departure window in eleven days; miss it, and the route to the edge closes for a decade. The station AI recommends quarantine and abandonment. Emotional beat: the first hard choice — stay safe, or go.

chapters.title: Children of the Deep
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The de-aged crew begin losing memories of their adult lives, forgetting skills, names, themselves. Elodie realizes her own memories are eroding fastest — except those of Ansel. Emotional beat: grief as a countdown; memory made mortal.

chapters.title: Eleven Days
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Preparations montage: cannibalizing station parts, teaching children to be passengers, patching the Meridian. Ansel and Elodie grow close through work, though she keeps mourning a version of him he never was. Emotional beat: bittersweet courtship under deadline.

chapters.title: Mutiny of the Small
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Two crew children, terrified, sabotage the launch rather than travel further from home. Elodie must reassert command over people who outrank her in years but not in memory. Emotional beat: leadership tested; authority without age.

chapters.title: Departure
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. They launch with hours to spare, leaving Vesper Gate dark behind them — Ansel abandons the only home he has left. He transmits a final log entry to no one. Emotional beat: severance; burning the bridge behind you.

chapters.title: The Silent Corridor
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. In transit, the ship passes relays that flicker awake as they approach, then die behind them — as if something is watching them pass. Elodie's childhood body begins failing; the reversal isn't stable. Emotional beat: mounting dread, flesh as evidence.

chapters.title: Ansel's Confession
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. He admits why he stayed at Vesper Gate: he once refused a transfer to be near someone who chose otherwise, and the silence afterward became his penance. Elodie tells him that in her future, he forgave himself. Emotional beat: vulnerability as turning point.

chapters.title: First Contact, Secondhand
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. The signal resolves partially: it is human-made, centuries old, a distress call from the first colony fleet — answered by something that learned to fold time around it. Emotional beat: awe curdling into horror; the listener is not malevolent, just vast.

chapters.title: The Cost of Answering
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Decoded instructions show the entity reverses time locally for anything that approaches it — the crew's de-aging was collateral kindness or collateral damage. To communicate, they must get closer, and closer means younger, then unborn. Emotional beat: terror of annihilation dressed as reunion.

chapters.title: Elodie's Equation
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Elodie works out that a tightly focused reply could be sent from the outer boundary without entering the reversal field — but it requires manual aiming from a hull position no adult could survive in radiation. A child's body, ironically, might. Emotional beat: sacrifice taking shape in numbers.

chapters.title: Arguments in the Dark
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Ansel refuses to let Elodie take the hull walk; she argues her memory of him is already the price paid, and she'd rather spend herself on purpose than fade by accident. The crew children vote. Emotional beat: love against duty, both sides right.

chapters.title: The Edge of Dead Space
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Arrival at the boundary: a region where starlight bends wrong and the ship's clocks run backward between seconds. They see the ancient fleet's hulk, preserved mid-scream, young again. Emotional beat: sublime dread; beauty at the edge of unmaking.

chapters.title: Hull Walk
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Elodie suits up while Ansel guides her over comms, their voices braided across the void. Radiation climbs; her memories shed in reverse — she forgets the future first, then begins forgetting him. Emotional beat: intimacy at maximum distance and maximum stakes.

chapters.title: The Signal Sent
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Elodie locks the array and sends humanity's answer — not a plea, but an introduction: who we were, who we are. The entity responds by stilling the reversal field, holding her in time. Emotional beat: triumph inseparable from loss.

chapters.title: What Was Forgotten
chapters.summary: Elodie's POV. Rescued inside, Elodie remembers nothing of Ansel — the price was exacted. She looks at this stranger who weeps with relief at her survival and cannot fathom why. Emotional beat: heartbreak rendered as blankness; love surviving its own erasure.

chapters.title: The Long Route Home
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The return journey: the entity, now addressed, opens stable corridors — the silent relays waking one by one as its gift. Ansel chooses not to tell Elodie what she gave up, only to stay beside her and let something new grow. Emotional beat: quiet hope after grief.

chapters.title: Vesper Gate, Alive
chapters.summary: Shared POV. They return to Vesper Gate, now a waystation on a speaking network, crewed by families of the restored. Elodie, older again by the entity's parting mercy, finds Ansel's old logs and reads her own name in them — and chooses him anyway, forward this time. Emotional beat: resolution; memory lost, love rebuilt.
